translationRepairs: Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Yan, who had served Jin as Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Zhou She, whose courtesy name was Shengyi, came from Ancheng in Runan and was the eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, who had served Jin as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
左光祿大夫 is indeed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, but the proposal leaves 顗 mistranscribed as Yan; the ancestor is Zhou Yi.
Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan, the eighth-generation descendant of Yan, Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Jin.
Zhou She, styled Shengyi, was a native of Ancheng in Runan and an eighth-generation descendant of Zhou Yi, the Jin Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
The office correction is right, but 顗 is Yi, not Yan. The revision corrects both the ancestor's name and 左光祿大夫.
In the Jianwu era, the Wei man Wu Bao came south and returned; he had Confucian learning, and the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Jiang Shi invited Bao to lecture.
In the Jianwu era, the Wei man Wu Bao returned south; he had Confucian learning, and the Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Jiang Shi invited Bao to lecture.
南歸 is one southward return or migration; the proposal correctly removes the duplicated motion in 'came south and returned.'
He was reappointed General of the Right Swift Cavalry and served concurrently as acting Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
He was reappointed General of the Right Swift Cavalry and served concurrently as acting Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
太子詹事 is Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, whereas Grand Tutor would be 太子太傅; the proposed office title is correct.
He was transferred to General of the Right Swift Cavalry and acted as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
He was transferred to General of the Right Swift Cavalry and acted as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
The literal field makes the same office error: 太子詹事 denotes the Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household, not a Grand Tutor.
An edict read: "Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou, She, has died suddenly, and my heart is full of grief.
An edict read: "Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou, She, has died suddenly, and my heart is full of grief.
The edict explicitly styles She 太子詹事; replacing the unrelated Grand Tutor title with Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household is accurate.
An edict said: "Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou She has suddenly met with death; my heart is pierced with sorrow.
An edict said: "Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household and Chief Rectifier of Yuzhou She has suddenly met with death; my heart is pierced with sorrow.
太子詹事 is correctly rendered as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household in the proposed literal replacement.
When he died he had no wife or concubine at home and no fields or house abroad. His two sons were left alone in poverty—a austerity that surpassed the stern worthies of old.
When he died he had no wife or concubine at home and no fields or house abroad. His two sons were left alone in poverty, and his austerity surpassed that of the stern worthies of old.
The article must be corrected, but 'an austerity that surpassed the stern worthies' compares a quality directly with people. The revision makes the comparison grammatical.
His grandfather Changzong was Aide on the March of the Song High Ancestor's hegemonial headquarters.
His grandfather Changzong was Acting Aide of the Song High Ancestor's hegemonial headquarters.
行參軍 is a staff aide post. The proposed Acting Aide removes the false phrase 'on the March' and correctly attaches the post to the hegemonial headquarters.
He had also mastered the writings of the hundred schools of thought and could draw on them all to avoid forbidden names.
He also possessed comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and took care to avoid all their taboo names.
百氏 in this personnel context means the various clans, but the proposal's 'hundred clan surnames' is overly literal and 'used them all' obscures that he avoided their taboo names.
He also mastered comprehensively the hundred schools, all of which he used for taboo avoidance.
He also had comprehensive knowledge of the various clans and avoided the taboo names of them all.
The proposal correctly rejects 'hundred schools,' but 百氏 refers to the various clans and 皆爲避諱 says that he observed their name taboos, not that he used surnames as a tool.
If after my death this too will be an item in the tradition."
After my death, this too will be an incident recorded in my biography."
The proposal notices the broken syntax but retains the awkward 'If after I die' and mistranslates 傳 as 'tradition.' The sentence anticipates an incident in his biography.

In the rites of seeing one off at the end, encoffining is set for a fixed day; wealthy houses with moistened roofs sometimes do it in half a day. Garments, covers, coffin, and outer coffin—taking speed as glory; kin, servants, and retainers each think of rest and return.

In the rites of seeing one off at the end, encoffining is set for a fixed day; wealthy households sometimes do it in half a day. Garments, covers, coffin, and outer coffin—taking speed as glory; kin, servants, and retainers each think of rest and return.
潤屋 invokes wealth adorning a house and modifies 豪家; 'wealthy households' correctly replaces the misleading literal calque 'moistened roofs.'

When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant and transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear General, Rectifier of his native district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.

When the High Ancestor ascended the throne, he was appointed Secretariat Attendant and transferred to General Who Establishes Might, Adviser to the Rear Army, Rectifier of his native district, and Left Assistant Director of the Secretariat.
後軍 is the Rear Army command qualified by 諮議參軍, not a person titled Rear General; the proposed wording corrects the object of 'Adviser.'
The texts of the Orchid Pavilion and Stone Chamber were exhausted for tent canopies.
The texts of the Orchid Terrace and Stone Chamber were entirely used up as tent coverings.
蘭臺 is correctly identified as the Orchid Terrace, but 'were exhausted for tent canopies' remains awkward English; 用盡於帷蓋 means the texts were used up as coverings.
Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yuan Yuling were also appointed to take part in deliberation.
Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were also appointed to take part in deliberation.
庾 is the surname Yu, so 庾於陵 is Yu Yuling. The proposal accurately removes the erroneous Yuan spelling from the idiomatic field.
Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yuan Yuling were again ordered to participate in consultation and knowledge.
Finally Zhou She, Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Yu Yuling were again ordered to participate in the deliberations.
Yu Yuling is the correct name, but 'participate in consultation and knowledge' remains an unnatural calque of 豫參知. The revision renders the coordinated appointment clearly.
The Zhou spoke of three thousand rites, reaching the full traditional count;
In the Zhou, the rites were said to number three thousand, a round total;
The original wrongly says Zhou 'spoke,' but the proposal remains awkward. 周代 supplies the era and 舉其盈數 explains three thousand as a cited round total.
This spring, as Your Majesty's carriage prepares to lead the armies in person, I searched through the military rites and reviewed their articles and regulations — all are comprehensive and complete.
Since this spring, as Your Majesty has prepared to lead the Six Armies in person, I have searched the military rites and reviewed their articles and regulations; all are comprehensive and complete.
自今春 and 六師 support 'since this spring' and 'Six Armies,' but the proposal's passive clauses and mixed tense are awkward. The memorial context permits the implied first-person agent.
Though this is not the same as the mound at Qufu, it may serve in some measure.
Though this differs from the case of Qinqiu (Sleeping Mound), it may serve as a rough likeness.
寢丘 is Qinqiu, the poor fief in the Sunshu Ao allusion, not Qufu. The proposed idiomatic replacement restores the place and the point of comparison.
Though the matter differs from sleeping on a mound, it may serve as a rough likeness.
Though the matter differs from Qinqiu, it may serve as a rough likeness.
寢丘 functions as the place-name Qinqiu in this allusion, not the verbal phrase 'sleeping on a mound'; the proposed literal replacement is accurate.
raise a mountain nine ren high and you regret even one basket spilled.
raise a mountain many ren high and you regret even one basket spilled.
累仞 means accumulating the mountain to many ren and supplies no numeral nine. The proposal removes a number imported from a related classical saying.
I, weeping through tears like snow, answered: "The enlightened meaning of 'long or short life,' Yannian and Wusheng's refined words — I have often heard them;
I answered, wiping away my tears: "I too have often heard the enlightened teaching concerning Pengzu and the short-lived, and the refined words of Wu's Prince of Yanling;
雪泣 means wiping tears, but the proposal still misreads 延吳 as two figures, 'Yan and Wu.' It abbreviates Wu's Prince of Yanling, Ji Zha; 彭殤 contrasts Pengzu with the short-lived.
